text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Scottish soldier LACHLAN MACQUARIE was born this day in 1762. He was appointed Governor of New South Wales to "improve the morals of the Colonists, encourage marriage and prohibit the use of spirituous liquors".
Judge Sir WILLIAM BURTON was born in 1794. He hanged 13 rebellious convicts on Norfolk Island in 1834, and was the first to rule that Australian Aborigines were subject to English Law.
Austrian composer FRANZ SCHUBERT was born on this day in 1797.
Bishop WILLIAM TYRRELL, Anglican Bishop of Newcastle where a street was named after him, was born in 1807.

Australian explorer THOMAS PETRIE was born in 1831. While still a child, he learnt aboriginal languages by travelling with tribes. He was the first white man to climb BUDERIM MOUNTAIN in Queensland, and opened-up the area to timber-cutting and farming.
ZANE GREY, the Ohio dentist who later became one of the most successful writers of Western novels, was born in 1875.
Legedary Russian ballerina ANNA PAVLOVA was born in 1885.
English screen and stage actress JEAN SIMMONS was born in 1929. No text received
American writer and novelist NORMAN MAILER was born on this day in 1923.
American tenor MARIO LANZA, who ruined a promising career with drugs and alcohol, was born in 1921.

US songwriter/ keyboard player and lead singer with 'K.C. and the Sunshine Band' HARRY WAYNE CASEY was born in 1951. With RICHARD FINCH they were the nucleus of the group and they wrote most of the hits. These included "Get Down Tonight" (1975), "That's the Way I Like It" (1975), "Shake Your Booty" (1976),
"Please Don't Go" (1979) and "Give It Up" (1983). In 1982 HARRY CASEY was seriously injured in a car accident but by 1983 he had recovered sufficiently to set up his own record company Meca.

British singer/songwriter JOHNNY ROTTEN (JOHN LYDON) was born in 1956. He was the co-founder of 'The Sex Pistols' in 1975. In 1977 they had a hit with "Good Save The Queen". JOHNNY left the group and formed his own band 'Public Image' and in 1983 they had a hit with "This Is Not A Love Song". The group then abbreviated the name to 'P.I.L.'.
** EVENTS **
1747 : The first clinic for the treatment of venereal
diseases was opened in London.
1865 : ROBERT E. LEE was appointed commander-in-chief of
Confederate forces. No text received
1876 : All American Indians were ordered onto
rservations.
1910 : The infamous Dr CRIPPEN poisoned his wife and
chopped her body into pieces, that he hid in their cellar.
1917 : The United States entered World War One, after
Germany torpedoed American ships.
1924 : The first winter Olympics came to end in the

French Alps. Competitors from 18 nations took part in week-long games. Most competitors were men with women only in the figure-skating events. Ironically it was the Scandinavians, who had opposed the establishment of the rival to their own Nordic Games, who dominated the medals table.
1925 : Two British anthrologists claimed Australian
Aborigines held a special place of significance in anthropology and the cultural history of the human race. Former British Museum authority Sir HERCULES READ, on a visit to Australia,

said the Aborigines had been able to maintain a stern form of discipline in their tribal law. He said they were a remarkable people who had maintained a wonderful system of life. Sir ARTHUR KEITH told the Royal College of Surgeons in London that when anthrologists sought a common ancestor for both black and white races, the Australian Aborigine came the closest to the ideal.
1929 : LEON TROTSKY was expelled from the Soviet Union,
after losing a power struggle with JOSEPH STALIN.
1943 : The RED ARMY re-captured Stalingrad, killing an
estimated 850,000 German troops. It was the worst single defeat in German history.
1950 : United States President HARRY TRUMAN gave the go
ahead for the development of the hydrogen bomb, which scientists say could be a thousand times more powerful than the bombs dropped on HIROSHIMA and NAGASAKI.
1956 : Creator of WINNIE THE POOH, A. A. MILNE, died.
1958 : The first satellite to orbit the Earth, EXPLORER
ONE, was launched from Cape Canaveral.
1974 : American film producer SAM GOLDWYN died.
1989 : Victoria's State deputy Premier ROBERT FORDHAM
quit over criticism of his handling of the Victorian Economic Development Corporation.
1994 : German luxury car-maker BMW announced the purchase
of Rover from British Aerospace, ending nearly a century of independent mass car production in Britain.
1995 : The death toll from a suicide bomb attack on
Algiers police headquarters rose to 42.
1996 : An explosion demolished an apartment building in
central Hunan province, China, killing 122 people.
